original_question: If g is a non-negative integer, is there an algorithm to decide whether or not a given locally flat PL-embedded surface of genus g in S^4 is unknotted?
target_in_paper: Section 7, concluding Question (3): "If g is a non-negative integer, is there an algorithm to decide whether or not a given locally flat PL-embedded surface of genus g in S^4 is unknotted?" The authors immediately add the conjectured answer: "No for any value of g."
correct_elements: The draft already matches the paper's final open Question (3) almost verbatim. It correctly fixes a non-negative genus g, stays in the locally flat PL category, uses S^4 as the ambient manifold, and asks for an algorithm deciding unknottedness.
missing_details: To make the question fully stand-alone, the surface should be identified explicitly as a closed connected orientable surface Σ_g of genus g; this is implicit in the phrase "surface of genus g" and consistent with the paper's surface-complement setting.
The quantifier is best made explicit as "for each fixed non-negative integer g" rather than a single uniform algorithm with g varying as part of the input.
Because this is an algorithmic question, one needs an implicit finite PL/combinatorial encoding of the embedded surface as input; the paper leaves that encoding unstated here.

For positive genus, the paper does not further define "unknotted" in the nearby text, so a stand-alone version should gloss it as equivalence to the standard genus-g embedding in S^4 while noting that this clarification is conventional rather than newly introduced by the paper.
The scope should remain exactly the locally flat PL category in S^4; it should not be broadened to smooth or purely topological embeddings, nor to surfaces in arbitrary 4-manifolds.
refined_question: For each fixed non-negative integer g, does there exist an algorithm that, given a finite PL description of a locally flat embedding Σ_g ↪ S^4 of a closed connected orientable surface Σ_g of genus g, decides whether the embedding is unknotted, i.e. PL-equivalent in S^4 to the standard genus-g embedding?
justification: The draft is already essentially exact: it reproduces the paper's concluding open Question (3) in Section 7 on page 167. The only sharpening needed is to make explicit the conventions that the paper has already fixed earlier: all embeddings are taken in the PL category and are locally flat (Section 2, opening paragraph, page 145), and the paper's surface-complement discussion concerns closed orientable surfaces in S^4 (Introduction, pages 143-145; Theorem 2.2, page 146). The nearby motivation is the geometric undecidability result proved for n-knots when K_n contains a group with unsolvable word problem (Theorem 7.1, page 164), together with the corollary that trivial n-knots are not algorithmically recognizable for n ≥ 3 (Corollary 7.2, page 167). The authors then pose this genus-g surface problem as the natural S^4 analogue that remains open, and conjecture a negative answer for every g. Since the paper does not supply a proved equivalent reformulation of this exact surface question, the faithful refinement should stay with the geometric decision problem itself and not broaden it.
